sections.title: Application
sections.description: The top-level application block defines the identity and requirements of your workflow application. It sets the name, version, and declares any required external capabilities.

optionalFields.name: version
optionalFields.description: Application version string (e.g. '1.0.0')

optionalFields.name: requires
optionalFields.description: List of required capabilities or feature flags

sections.example:
name: my-app
version: "1.0.0"
requires:
  - messaging
  - database
relationships: The application name is used as a namespace for module resolution
Required capabilities must be satisfied by the platform configuration

sections.title: Modules
sections.description: Modules are the building blocks of a workflow application. Each module represents a runtime service component such as an HTTP server, database connection, message broker, or pipeline step.

requiredFields.name: name
requiredFields.description: Unique identifier for this module instance

optionalFields.name: config
optionalFields.description: Type-specific configuration key-value pairs

optionalFields.name: dependsOn
optionalFields.description: Module names this module depends on — controls initialization order

optionalFields.name: branches
optionalFields.description: Conditional routing to other modules

sections.example:
modules:
  - name: api-server
    type: http.server
    config:
      address: ":8080"
  - name: db
    type: database.workflow
    config:
      driver: postgres
      dsn: "${DATABASE_URL}"
    dependsOn:
      - api-server
relationships: Modules are referenced by workflows.http.routes[].handler
Modules can reference pipelines via their config
Module names must be unique across all imported files

sections.title: Workflows
sections.description: The workflows section groups all event-driven entrypoints into your application. It contains sub-sections for HTTP, messaging, state machine, and event-based workflows.

optionalFields.name: http
optionalFields.description: HTTP server and router configuration

optionalFields.name: messaging
optionalFields.description: Message broker subscriptions and topics

optionalFields.name: statemachine
optionalFields.description: State machine engine definitions and transitions

optionalFields.name: events
optionalFields.description: Event processor handlers and adapters

sections.example:
workflows:
  http:
    server: api-server
    router: api-router
    routes:
      - method: GET
        path: /health
        handler: health-check
relationships: Workflow handlers reference module names defined in the modules section
Routes can inline pipeline definitions or reference named pipelines

sections.title: Workflows > HTTP
sections.description: HTTP workflow configuration defines an HTTP server, router, route table, and optional middleware chains. Routes map HTTP methods and paths to handler modules or inline pipelines.

requiredFields.name: server
requiredFields.description: Name of the http.server module to bind routes to

optionalFields.name: router
optionalFields.description: Name of the http.router module

optionalFields.name: routes
optionalFields.description: List of route definitions (method, path, handler/pipeline)

optionalFields.name: middleware
optionalFields.description: Ordered list of middleware module names applied to all routes

sections.example:
workflows:
  http:
    server: api-server
    router: api-router
    middleware:
      - auth-middleware
    routes:
      - method: POST
        path: /users
        pipeline:
          steps:
            - name: validate
              type: step.validate
            - name: create-user
              type: step.db_query
relationships: server must reference a module of type http.server
router must reference a module of type http.router
middleware entries must reference modules of a middleware-compatible type

sections.title: Workflows > Messaging
sections.description: Messaging workflows connect your application to message brokers. Define subscriptions that trigger pipelines when messages arrive on configured topics.

requiredFields.name: broker
requiredFields.description: Name of the messaging broker module

optionalFields.name: subscriptions
optionalFields.description: List of topic subscriptions with pipeline handlers

optionalFields.name: topics
optionalFields.description: Topic definitions for publishing

sections.example:
workflows:
  messaging:
    broker: kafka-broker
    subscriptions:
      - topic: user-events
        group: user-processor
        pipeline:
          steps:
            - name: process
              type: step.transform
relationships: broker must reference a module of a messaging broker type
Subscription pipelines follow the same step schema as HTTP route pipelines

sections.title: Workflows > State Machine
sections.description: State machine workflows define finite state automata with named states and transition conditions. The engine processes events and drives state transitions.

requiredFields.name: engine
requiredFields.description: Name of the state machine engine module

optionalFields.name: definitions
optionalFields.description: Named state machine definitions with states and transitions

sections.example:
workflows:
  statemachine:
    engine: order-sm
    definitions:
      - name: order-lifecycle
        initial: pending
        states:
          - name: pending
            on:
              CONFIRM: confirmed
          - name: confirmed
            on:
              SHIP: shipped
relationships: engine must reference a module of type statemachine.engine
State names must be unique within a definition

sections.title: Workflows > Events
sections.description: Event workflows respond to domain events via an event processor module. Handlers map event types to pipeline handlers.

requiredFields.name: processor
requiredFields.description: Name of the event processor module

optionalFields.name: handlers
optionalFields.description: List of event type to pipeline mappings

optionalFields.name: adapters
optionalFields.description: Adapter module names for event source integration

sections.example:
workflows:
  events:
    processor: event-bus
    handlers:
      - event: user.created
        pipeline:
          steps:
            - name: send-welcome
              type: step.http_request
relationships: processor must reference a module of type events.processor
Event names are matched against the processor's configured event schema

sections.title: Pipelines
sections.description: Pipelines are named sequences of steps that process data through transformations, queries, HTTP calls, and flow control. They can be defined inline in workflows or as named top-level reusable pipelines.

optionalFields.name: timeout
optionalFields.description: Maximum duration for the entire pipeline (e.g. '30s')

optionalFields.name: retry
optionalFields.description: Retry policy for transient failures

sections.example:
pipelines:
  create-user:
    steps:
      - name: validate-input
        type: step.validate
        config:
          schema: user-schema
      - name: insert-record
        type: step.db_query
        config:
          query: "INSERT INTO users ..."
      - name: publish-event
        type: step.publish
        config:
          topic: user-events
relationships: Named pipelines can be referenced by workflows using 'pipeline: ref: <name>'
Steps can use template expressions like '{{ .input.field }}' to reference previous step outputs
Steps of type step.branch enable conditional flow control

sections.title: Triggers
sections.description: Triggers define how external events initiate pipeline execution. Supported trigger types include HTTP (inline), cron schedules, and domain events.

optionalFields.name: schedule
optionalFields.description: Cron expression for scheduled triggers (e.g. '0 * * * *')

optionalFields.name: event
optionalFields.description: Event name to listen for (event triggers)

optionalFields.name: pipeline
optionalFields.description: Pipeline to execute when triggered

sections.example:
triggers:
  - type: cron
    schedule: "0 9 * * MON-FRI"
    pipeline:
      ref: daily-report
  - type: event
    event: user.signup
    pipeline:
      ref: welcome-flow
relationships: Cron triggers run in the UTC timezone by default
Referenced pipelines must be defined in the top-level pipelines section

sections.title: Imports
sections.description: Imports allow splitting a large workflow configuration across multiple YAML files. Imported files are merged at runtime, enabling modular organization of modules, pipelines, and workflows.

requiredFields.name: file
requiredFields.description: Relative path to the imported YAML file

optionalFields.name: alias
optionalFields.description: Optional namespace alias for imported resources

relationships: Imported files are resolved relative to the importing file's directory
Module names must remain unique across all imported files
Circular imports are not supported

sections.title: Config Providers
sections.description: Config providers supply configuration values to modules at startup. They support static defaults, environment variables, and external file sources. Multiple providers are merged in order.

optionalFields.name: values
optionalFields.description: Static key-value pairs (type: defaults)

optionalFields.name: prefix
optionalFields.description: Environment variable prefix to strip (type: env)

optionalFields.name: path
optionalFields.description: Path to the config file (type: file)

optionalFields.name: format
optionalFields.description: File format: 'yaml', 'json', 'toml' (type: file)

sections.example:
configProviders:
  - type: defaults
    values:
      port: 8080
      logLevel: info
  - type: env
    prefix: APP_
  - type: file
    path: ./config.local.yaml
    format: yaml
relationships: Later providers override values from earlier providers
Environment variable names are uppercased and dots replaced with underscores

sections.title: Platform / Infrastructure / Sidecars
sections.description: Infrastructure-as-code sections declare the deployment environment for your workflow application. These sections are consumed by the platform layer to provision resources, configure networking, and attach sidecar services.

optionalFields.name: platform
optionalFields.description: Target runtime platform configuration

optionalFields.name: infrastructure
optionalFields.description: Cloud resources (databases, queues, storage) to provision

optionalFields.name: sidecars
optionalFields.description: Auxiliary containers to run alongside the application

sections.example:
platform:
  type: kubernetes
  namespace: production
  replicas: 3

infrastructure:
  postgres:
    type: rds
    size: db.t3.medium

sidecars:
  - name: metrics-exporter
    image: prom/node-exporter:latest
relationships: Platform configuration is environment-specific and typically sourced via config providers
Infrastructure resources are referenced by modules via their names
